name: CardiacLens v9.10.347.205
notes: Replaced the small bottom toast used for newly-missed events with the same full event action card already used for on-demand Run from the Events widget. Missed events now show one at a time, in time order, advancing automatically once each one is resolved (all actions logged, Done, or Save as Missed).

Removed the v9.10.347.204 attempt at a chime on the missed-event alert. iOS blocks audio from firing without a direct tap or touch attached, and the app becoming visible again does not count as one, so the previous attempt was reliably silent. No sound plays for the missed-event card. Sound for on-time reminders while the app is already open is unchanged.

OS-level notifications now carry which scheduled event they were for. Tapping a real notification opens that event's action card directly, whether CardiacLens was already open or fully closed, instead of only focusing the app on whatever screen it was last showing. If the specific event can no longer be resolved (edited or deleted since the notification went out), it opens the Events queue instead.
The medicine-due-today reminder is routed separately from scheduled events, since it has no matching entry in the event list; tapping it opens Log Medicine directly.

sw.js notificationclick now reads the event tag from the notification payload and either messages an already-open app tab or opens a new window with the tag in the URL for a fully-closed app, so both cases route to the right screen.

Corrected a separate, pre-existing version-drift bug found while working this release: this app has 8+ live current-version display locations (documented in its own embedded release checklist), and 6 of them (CURRENT_VERSION var, Settings panel version display, and 4 Doctor's Report / Advanced Analytics footer strings) had been stuck at v9.10.347.197 since that release, unnoticed through v9.10.347.198-204. All 6 now correctly read v9.10.347.205. This bug predates this session's changes and was not introduced by the notification fix.

This does not change detection: an event is still only treated as missed if discovered within 90 minutes of its scheduled time, and daily state still resets at midnight or on the next app open after a day rollover, same as before this release.

This does not add real background delivery. If CardiacLens is fully closed and the phone stays locked and untouched, nothing fires until the app is reopened, same underlying limitation documented in v9.10.347.204. That gap requires real Web Push and remains separate, larger work.
label: MissedEventCardAndTapRouting
summary: Missed events now open the real per-event action card, one at a time, instead of a small toast with no tap behavior. Real OS notifications now route taps to the specific event instead of just opening the app. No sound is attempted for missed-event alerts, since iOS blocks it without a direct gesture.
fixes: Missed-event alert replaced: full action card instead of small unlinked toast, sequential queue instead of a single silent notice.
Notification tap routing: sw.js and the app now hand off which event was tapped, opening that event's card instead of just the app root.
Dropped the non-functional forced chime attempt from v9.10.347.204 rather than leaving broken audio code in place.
testing: node --check passed on all.js, sw.js, and every inline <script> block in index.html (10 blocks).

Verified index.html inline script and all.js received byte-identical new/changed function bodies (fireOSNotification, hideModal, runCatchUpScan plus the new _queueMissedEvents, _advanceMissedEventQueue, _maybeAdvanceMissedQueue, _clResolveEventByTag, _clOpenEventFromTag, _clCheckOpenEventParam, and the SW message listener), by direct diff of both files.
Verified no em dashes in any newly added code, comments, or Help content.

Ran a headless Playwright build against the actual built index.html (Chromium): seeded two past-due dailyPlan events and called the real runCatchUpScan(). Confirmed the earlier-time event opened as the full action card (not a toast), confirmed the second event stayed queued and untouched, confirmed Done - Dismiss on the first auto-advanced to the second after the intended delay, and confirmed the app returned to a fully closed, empty-queue state after the second was dismissed. Zero page errors across the run.

Ran a second Playwright pass specifically on the multi-action reshow edge case: tapped one action of a two-action event and confirmed the SAME card reshows with that action grayed out, and the queued second event is NOT advanced early. Only advances once the card is genuinely resolved.

Ran a third pass calling _clResolveEventByTag directly against all five tag shapes the app actually produces (dailyPlan-based, settings.dailyEvents id-based, legacy name-based, medicine-reminder, and an unresolvable tag). All five resolved to the correct event or correctly returned null.

Not tested on a real device and not tested against the real Notification/Service Worker click path (that requires a genuine push and a real iOS home-screen install, which this environment can't simulate) - the sw.js and message-listener logic is verified by syntax and code review only, not by an actual tap on a real lock-screen banner. Confirm this specific path on your iPhone before relying on it.

Known limitation, called out directly: tag-to-event matching is string-pattern based across the several tag formats already in the codebase (id-based and name-based), not a single canonical lookup. Falls back to opening the Events queue if a tag can't be resolved, rather than failing silently.
